answer.rationale: Contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew and the line sits at 94% with no buffer, so switch, second-source, or defer would raise delivery risk (c5 was non-critical month-to-month and does not clearly apply). Staying with the incumbent preserves integration and deliveries (c1); cost pressure is applied via renewal benchmarking and possible term-for-price (c4, c6) rather than a bare renew. Verifying c4 (how much margin was actually recovered) and c2 (whether last year's switch was truly low-risk/quick) before locking the action. Uncertain an 18% cut is feasible without scope or service giveaways.
